title: Databricks’ new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth
slides: Can Databricks' agent tell Ali Ghodsi the truth?
It reviews the company's own operations data daily.
But it surfaces problems executives never asked about.
Leaders using such agents get harder questions sooner.
Ask your data one uncomfortable question this week.
thread_text:
1. The AI That Questions CEOs

Databricks built an agent that reviews its own operations daily. It doesn't wait for executives to ask — it surfaces problems they never thought to look for.

2. The Agent's Daily Grind

Every day, it scans the company's operational data. No prompts from leaders. No specific questions. Just a constant, silent audit of everything.

3. Uncomfortable Discoveries

The agent finds issues executives never asked about. Not because they forgot, but because they didn't know what to ask. It reveals blind spots.

4. Hard Questions, Sooner

Leaders using such agents get confronted with tough questions faster. The agent doesn't soften the blow — it delivers the truth upfront.

5. Your Turn to Ask

This week, ask your data one uncomfortable question. Something you've been avoiding. See what it tells you — and act on it.

instagram.caption:
Databricks built an AI agent that reviews its own operations every single day — and it reports straight to CEO Ali Ghodsi. 🧠

It scans the company's operational data daily, with no prompts from leaders.

It surfaces problems executives never thought to ask about — not because they forgot, but because they didn't know what to ask.

Leaders using agents like this get the hard questions sooner, unsoftened.

If you work with data or content, the lesson is blunt: your blind spots are now auditable, every day. 👀

So this week — what's the one uncomfortable question about your own work you've been avoiding asking your data? 💬
